title: Batch messages for a bulk API
summary: Split a stream of messages into batches limited by both count and UTF-8 size.
prompt: A bulk ingestion endpoint accepts at most `maxCount` messages and at most `maxBytes` bytes of
List<List<string>> Batch(IEnumerable<string> messages, int maxCount, int maxBytes)
- Keep the messages **in order**; fill each batch as far as both limits allow, then start the next.
- Size is the message's **UTF-8 byte count** (`"héllo"` is 6 bytes, not 5 characters).
- A batch exactly at a limit is fine.
- A single message bigger than `maxBytes` goes in a batch **on its own** (let the API reject it).
- Never produce an empty batch; no messages gives an empty list.
starter: List<List<string>> Batch(IEnumerable<string> messages, int maxCount, int maxBytes)
solution: List<List<string>> Batch(IEnumerable<string> messages, int maxCount, int maxBytes)
template: string DojoShow(List<List<string>> batches) => string.Join(" | ", batches.Select(b => "[" + string.Join(",", b) + "]"));
Dojo.Eq("byte limit, filled exactly to the limit", "[aaaa,bbbb] | [cc,dddddd]", DojoShow(Batch(new[] { "aaaa", "bbbb", "cc", "dddddd" }, 10, 8)));
Dojo.Eq("bytes are UTF-8 bytes, not characters", "[héllo] | [wörld]", DojoShow(Batch(new[] { "héllo", "wörld" }, 10, 11)));
Dojo.Eq("an oversized message goes alone, with no empty batch", "[123456789012] | [x,y]", DojoShow(Batch(new[] { "123456789012", "x", "y" }, 10, 5)));
wrong: List<List<string>> Batch(IEnumerable<string> messages, int maxCount, int maxBytes)
List<List<string>> Batch(IEnumerable<string> messages, int maxCount, int maxBytes)
hints: Walk the messages once, keeping the current batch and its running byte total.
Before adding a message, close the current batch if adding it would break either limit, but only if the batch is not empty.
`Encoding.UTF8.GetByteCount(message)` gives the size the API counts.
